v3 Local-First Vault Architecture

Canonical source of truth: ~/RajAI/Vault on Zorin OS. Colab receives a temporary snapshot at startup and returns runtime-created memories, OCR results, compiled book data, and Inbox decisions through explicit or automatic sync.
Zorin canonical Vault ~/RajAI/Vault/state/vault-export.json ~/RajAI/Vault/sources/ ~/RajAI/Vault/incoming/ │ │ seed snapshot + pending sources ▼ Colab runtime cache /content/rajai_memory_cache │ │ OCR / compile / memory changes ▼ Periodic pull + final pull before stop │ ▼ Merged canonical Vault on Zorin

Automatic source discovery

Drop files under ~/RajAI/Vault/incoming/COLLECTION/. The first directory below incoming becomes the collection. New files are hashed, copied into managed local storage, queued, and uploaded during the next start or Vault sync.

~/RajAI/Vault/incoming/projects/architecture.pdf ~/RajAI/Vault/incoming/books/Fire_Blood_ASOIF.epub ~/RajAI/Vault/incoming/conversations/rajai-history.html

Account-independent operation

The same Local-First Vault can seed a manually selected Colab account without re-running every historical ingest command. The CLI does not automatically rotate Google accounts; account selection remains an explicit operator action.

Syntax Conventions

NotationMeaningExample
[OPTION]Optional argument. Omit it to use the configured/default behaviour.rajai-colab status [--verbose]
VALUEReplace the uppercase placeholder with a real value.--model qwen3:8b
A|B|CChoose exactly one accepted value.--runtime t4|cpu|tpu-v5e1
...More than one word or repeated element can follow.rajai-colab help vault ingest
\ at line endShell line continuation. The next physical line is part of the same command.rajai-colab start \
--runtime t4
Quoted textUse quotes around values containing spaces or shell-special characters."Project notes"
~The current Linux user's home directory.~/Documents/file.pdf
Shell safety
  • Do not copy comments or surrounding prose into the terminal.
  • Review destructive options such as --force, --replace, stop, restart, rotate-key, forget, and reject before running them.
  • Do not place secrets directly in commands because shell history may retain them.

Architecture and Command Flow

The CLI runs on Zorin OS and controls an explicitly selected Google Colab runtime. It publishes the authenticated backend through a Cloudflare tunnel and updates the fixed GitHub Pages endpoint manifest. Zorin is the canonical source of truth for the owner-only Local-First Vault; Colab /content is a temporary fast cache, while Google Drive is optional for models, application data, or a secondary mirror.

Recommended Operator Workflow

INSTALL / UPGRADE → rajai-colab --version → rajai-colab migrate-config --force → rajai-colab auth --reset --email ACCOUNT@gmail.com → rajai-colab doctor → optional: rajai-colab diagnose-allocation --gpu T4 → rajai-colab start --runtime t4 --model general → rajai-colab status --verbose → rajai-colab key (guest) → rajai-colab key --owner (private owner) → use the fixed GitHub Pages UI → rajai-colab logs / repair as needed → rajai-colab stop

Command Summary

CommandFamilyPurpose
rajai-colab --versionGeneralPrints the installed RajAIAssist CLI version and exits without contacting Colab, GitHub, Drive, Ollama, or the active backend.
rajai-colab helpHelpDisplays the built-in workflow guide or a detailed guide for one supported help topic.
rajai-colab cheatsheetHelpPrints a compact one-page command reference grouped into setup, start, operate, models, Vault, and help workflows.
rajai-colab initSetupCreates the RajAIAssist configuration and private secrets files in the user configuration directory.
rajai-colab migrate-configSetupNormalizes an older RajAIAssist configuration into the v3.0.0 Local-First schema while retaining compatible custom settings and creating a backup.
rajai-colab authIdentity and AccessAuthorizes the official Google Colab CLI, verifies OAuth scopes, and binds RajAIAssist to one expected Google account.
rajai-colab doctorDiagnosticsRuns a preflight assessment of configuration, secrets, GitHub access, Colab identity, active assignments, notifications, sleep inhibition, runtime profiles, and Vault configuration.
rajai-colab diagnose-allocationDiagnosticsRequests one isolated real GPU runtime, inspects it, and immediately releases it without mounting Drive or starting RajAIAssist services.
rajai-colab notify-testDiagnosticsTests Zorin desktop notification delivery using the local notification mechanism.
rajai-colab startLifecycleCreates and bootstraps one explicitly selected Colab runtime, model server, authenticated backend, Cloudflare tunnel, GitHub endpoint manifest, and optional detached supervisor.
rajai-colab statusLifecycleDisplays lifecycle, runtime, model, service health, manifest signature, Vault availability, supervisor, and optional diagnostics.
rajai-colab keyIdentity and AccessPrints the disposable guest lifecycle key, or the private owner key when --owner is specified.
rajai-colab openLifecycleOpens the permanent GitHub Pages URL using the default local web browser and prints the URL.
rajai-colab logsLifecycleDisplays the local availability-supervisor log and optionally retrieves active-provider process, health, and remote log information.
rajai-colab repairLifecycleAttempts to repair the current provider services while preserving lifecycle keys; when provider repair fails, it can request a replacement of the same selected runtime.
rajai-colab rotate-keyIdentity and AccessRotates both owner and guest lifecycle keys by stopping and rebuilding the selected provider while keeping the current runtime/model policy.
rajai-colab stopLifecyclePublishes the endpoint offline, stops the selected Colab provider and supervisor, clears local lifecycle state, and leaves the persistent configuration, secrets, Drive data, and Vault intact.
rajai-colab restartLifecycleStops the current lifecycle and starts a fresh selected runtime with new owner and guest keys.
rajai-colab models listModelsLists built-in T4/CPU Ollama aliases, experimental TPU aliases, configured defaults, and the active lifecycle model.
rajai-colab models currentModelsShows the configured default models for T4, CPU, and TPU, plus the active lifecycle model when one exists.
rajai-colab models setModelsChanges the persistent T4/Ollama default model in config.toml. It does not switch the currently active lifecycle.
rajai-colab models verifyModelsValidates a model tag and, when a lifecycle is active, queries the remote model server to check whether the model is available.
rajai-colab vault initMemory VaultInitializes or verifies the owner-only Zorin-canonical Local-First Vault and discovers new files under incoming collection folders.
rajai-colab vault statusMemory VaultReports Vault availability, cache/persistent paths, records, approved memories, sources, chunks, Inbox counts, and collections.
rajai-colab vault ingestMemory VaultCopies a local file into the canonical Zorin Vault, queues it by content hash, and synchronizes it to the active Colab cache for extraction, OCR, book processing, and evidence indexing when available.
rajai-colab vault compileMemory VaultRebuilds compiled metadata/indexes for selected Vault sources and can optionally ask the active model to create chapter/source summaries.
rajai-colab vault searchMemory VaultSearches approved structured memories and compiled Vault source evidence using the owner-only retrieval endpoint.
rajai-colab vault listMemory VaultLists structured memory records by collection and lifecycle status.
rajai-colab vault rememberMemory VaultCreates an explicit owner-approved memory record. It bypasses the suggestion Inbox because the owner entered it directly.
rajai-colab vault correctMemory VaultCreates a corrected memory version while retaining the previous record as superseded history.
rajai-colab vault forgetMemory VaultMarks a memory as forgotten so it is excluded from normal retrieval while retaining the audit and historical record.
rajai-colab vault suggestMemory VaultReviews one browser chat with the active model and creates owner-reviewable candidate memories in the Vault Inbox.
rajai-colab vault inboxMemory VaultLists model-suggested memory candidates and their review status.
rajai-colab vault decideMemory VaultApproves or rejects one pending Inbox memory. Approval creates a separate approved memory record; rejection keeps only audit history.
rajai-colab vault exportMemory VaultWrites the current canonical Zorin Vault manifest, structured memories, source metadata/chunks, and Inbox as one protected JSON export.
rajai-colab vault syncLocal-First VaultShows sync state or pushes, pulls, and reconciles the Zorin-canonical Vault with the active Colab cache.
rajai-colab vault import-chatLocal-First VaultImports a conversation export as redacted source evidence and optionally synchronizes it to the active runtime.
General

rajai-colab --version

Prints the installed RajAIAssist CLI version and exits without contacting Colab, GitHub, Drive, Ollama, or the active backend.

Syntax

rajai-colab --version

What the command does

  • Loads the installed command entry point.
  • Prints the application version string.
  • Returns immediately.

Arguments and options

No command-specific arguments.

Examples

Example 1: Check the installed version

rajai-colab --version

Use after installing or upgrading the wheel.

Example 2: Confirm the executable and version

command -v rajai-colab
rajai-colab --version

Verifies which executable is on PATH before printing its version.

Example 3: Record the version in a support log

rajai-colab --version | tee ~/Documents/rajai-version.txt

Saves the version for troubleshooting or change records.

Expected outcomes
  • Expected output resembles: 3.0.0-cli.

Syntax

What the command does

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault

Examples

Example 1: Show the help index

rajai-colab help

Cautions
  • Only built-in topics are accepted; use rajai-colab COMMAND --help for the exact argparse option list.

Setup

rajai-colab init

Creates the RajAIAssist configuration and private secrets files in the user configuration directory.

Syntax

rajai-colab init [--force]

What the command does

  • Creates required directories.
  • Writes a default config.toml.
  • Writes a private secrets.json template and prints next steps.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
--forceOptional flagReplace existing configuration and secrets files. Use only after making backups.False

Examples

Example 1: First-time initialization

rajai-colab init

Creates files only when they do not already exist.

Example 2: Recreate defaults after backups

cp ~/.config/rajai-colab/config.toml ~/Documents/config.toml.backup
cp ~/.config/rajai-colab/secrets.json ~/Documents/secrets.json.backup
rajai-colab init --force

Replaces both files after explicit backups.

Example 3: Initialize and secure the secrets file

rajai-colab init
chmod 600 ~/.config/rajai-colab/secrets.json

Creates the files and restricts secrets to the owner account.

Cautions
  • --force can replace configured account, model, Vault, and GitHub settings.
  • Never commit secrets.json to GitHub.

Related commands: rajai-colab migrate-config · rajai-colab auth · rajai-colab doctor

Setup

rajai-colab migrate-config

Normalizes an older RajAIAssist configuration into the v3.0.0 Local-First schema while retaining compatible custom settings and creating a backup.

Syntax

rajai-colab migrate-config [--force]

What the command does

  • Detects retired or legacy keys.
  • Loads and validates the effective configuration.
  • Writes a clean v3.0.0 Local-First config.toml and keeps a timestamped backup.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
--forceOptional flagWrite a normalized file even when no migration notes are detected.False

Examples

Example 1: Normal migration after an upgrade

rajai-colab migrate-config

Writes a clean file when legacy settings are detected.

Example 2: Force normalization

rajai-colab migrate-config --force

Useful after a hotfix or when a previously written profile needs to be repaired.

Example 3: Inspect important values after migration

rajai-colab migrate-config --force
grep -nE "default_runtime|default_model|context_tokens|max_output_tokens|vault_enabled" ~/.config/rajai-colab/config.toml

Confirms key runtime and Vault settings.

Cautions
  • Run this with the same Linux user that owns ~/.config/rajai-colab.
  • Review the generated backup before deleting it.

Identity and Access

rajai-colab auth

Authorizes the official Google Colab CLI, verifies OAuth scopes, and binds RajAIAssist to one expected Google account.

Syntax

rajai-colab auth [--reset] [--email ACCOUNT@gmail.com] [--force]

What the command does

  • Optionally stops the named RajAIAssist lifecycle.
  • Optionally removes cached OAuth and Colab session metadata.
  • Runs or validates the official Colab OAuth flow.
  • Compares the authenticated email with the expected email.
  • Stores the verified account in config.toml and reports active assignments.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
--resetOptional flagRemove cached OAuth and local Colab session metadata before authorizing again.False
--email EMAILOptional valueExpected Google account email. A verified value is persisted to config.toml.Existing bound account, or the authenticated identity.
--forceOptional flagWhen resetting authentication, stop the named RajAIAssist lifecycle first. Unknown browser runtimes are not stopped automatically.False

Prerequisites

  • The official colab command must be installed.
  • Complete the browser consent flow with the exact intended Google account.

Examples

Example 1: Bind the first account

rajai-colab auth --reset --email raj@example.com

Starts a clean OAuth flow and binds the verified account.

Example 2: Reauthenticate the currently configured account

rajai-colab auth --reset --email raj@example.com

Use when the OAuth token expired or the wrong account was selected.

Example 3: Force-reset after stopping the named lifecycle

rajai-colab auth --reset --email raj@example.com --force

Stops the named RajAI lifecycle before clearing cached identity data.

Cautions
  • The command refuses to delete unknown browser-created assignments.
  • Authorization codes and OAuth tokens are secrets.
  • Account selection in Chrome does not prove which account the CLI is using.

Related commands: rajai-colab doctor · rajai-colab diagnose-allocation · rajai-colab start

Diagnostics

rajai-colab doctor

Runs a preflight assessment of configuration, secrets, GitHub access, Colab identity, active assignments, notifications, sleep inhibition, runtime profiles, and Vault configuration.

Syntax

rajai-colab doctor

What the command does

  • Loads and validates config.toml.
  • Validates secrets.json permissions and required values.
  • Checks the official Colab CLI and authenticated identity.
  • Checks GitHub repository access.
  • Reports active assignments, warnings, and blocking problems.

Arguments and options

No command-specific arguments.

Examples

Example 1: Standard preflight

rajai-colab doctor

Run before every first start after installation, migration, or reauthentication.

Example 2: Save the diagnostic report

rajai-colab doctor | tee ~/Documents/rajai-doctor.txt

Captures the complete preflight result for troubleshooting.

Example 3: Use as a shell gate

if rajai-colab doctor; then
  echo "RajAIAssist is ready to start"
else
  echo "Resolve doctor problems first"
fi

Runs start automation only when the preflight returns success.

Expected outcomes
  • Returns 0 when ready, 1 when blocking problems exist.
  • Warnings do not necessarily prevent startup.

Related commands: rajai-colab auth · rajai-colab diagnose-allocation · rajai-colab status

Diagnostics

rajai-colab diagnose-allocation

Requests one isolated real GPU runtime, inspects it, and immediately releases it without mounting Drive or starting RajAIAssist services.

Syntax

rajai-colab diagnose-allocation [--gpu TYPE] [--yes] [--timeout SECONDS]

What the command does

  • Verifies account binding and confirms there is no active lifecycle or assignment.
  • Creates a temporary Colab state file.
  • Requests one GPU assignment.
  • Reports success or a classified failure.
  • Stops the probe and removes temporary state.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
--gpu TYPEOptional valueGPU accelerator to request. Accepted values / range: T4, L4, G4, A100, H100.Configured GPU, normally T4.
--yesOptional flagSkip the interactive confirmation.False
--timeout SECONDSOptional integerMaximum allocation wait in seconds. Accepted values / range: Positive integer.900

Prerequisites

  • No RajAIAssist lifecycle may be active.
  • No browser-created or unrelated Colab assignment may be active.

Examples

Example 1: Interactive T4 diagnostic

rajai-colab diagnose-allocation --gpu T4

Prompts before requesting a real T4.

Example 2: Non-interactive T4 diagnostic

rajai-colab diagnose-allocation --gpu T4 --yes

Useful when the operator already understands the allocation side effect.

Example 3: Longer diagnostic timeout

rajai-colab diagnose-allocation --gpu T4 --yes --timeout 1200

Allows up to 20 minutes for the probe.

Cautions
  • This consumes a real allocation briefly.
  • HTTP 503 does not prove quota exhaustion; it can also mean temporary capacity or control-plane issues.

Related commands: rajai-colab doctor · rajai-colab start · rajai-colab status

Lifecycle

rajai-colab start

Creates and bootstraps one explicitly selected Colab runtime, model server, authenticated backend, Cloudflare tunnel, GitHub endpoint manifest, and optional detached supervisor.

Syntax

rajai-colab start [--replace] [--runtime t4|cpu|tpu-v5e1] [--model MODEL] [--context TOKENS] [--max-output TOKENS] [--no-drive] [--no-monitor] [--open]

What the command does

  • Loads configuration and secrets.
  • Verifies the bound Google account and refuses unrelated active assignments.
  • Resolves runtime and model profiles.
  • Creates owner and guest lifecycle keys.
  • Allocates the selected runtime.
  • Optionally mounts Drive.
  • Uploads and executes the remote bootstrap.
  • Starts model server, backend, tunnel, manifest, and supervisor.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
--replaceOptional flagStop and replace an existing named RajAIAssist lifecycle.False
--runtime TYPEOptional valueRuntime provider for this lifecycle. Accepted values / range: t4, cpu, tpu-v5e1.config.toml default_runtime
--model MODELOptional valueBuilt-in alias, exact Ollama tag, or TPU Hugging Face identifier.Runtime-specific configured default.
--context TOKENSOptional integerOne-lifecycle context-window override. Must satisfy runtime validation.Runtime-specific configured context.
--max-output TOKENSOptional integerOne-lifecycle output-token ceiling. Must be lower than the selected context.Runtime-specific configured maximum.
--no-driveOptional flagSkip the interactive Google Drive mount request. The Local-First Vault can still be seeded from Zorin; Drive-backed model reuse and optional application-data persistence may be unavailable.False
--no-monitorOptional flagDo not launch the detached availability supervisor.False
--openOptional flagOpen the permanent GitHub Pages URL after startup.False

Prerequisites

  • doctor should report ready.
  • The selected account must have no unrelated active assignment.
  • GitHub token must have Contents read/write access to the configured repository.

Examples

Example 1: Recommended T4 general-assistant lifecycle

rajai-colab start --runtime t4 --model general

Uses qwen3:8b with the configured adaptive T4 context profile.

Example 2: Coding lifecycle with 32K context and 8K output

rajai-colab start \
  --runtime t4 \
  --model coding \
  --context 32768 \
  --max-output 8192 \
  --open

Uses qwen2.5-coder:7b and opens the fixed UI after startup.

Example 3: Explicit CPU lifecycle

rajai-colab start --runtime cpu --model qwen3:1.7b --context 8192 --max-output 4096

Starts Ollama on a standard Colab CPU runtime. CPU mode is slower and is never selected automatically.

Example 4: Experimental TPU lifecycle

rajai-colab start --runtime tpu-v5e1 --model tpu-default

Starts the experimental JAX/Flax TPU server rather than Ollama.

Cautions
  • TPU mode is experimental.
  • Large context/output values increase memory use and latency.
  • --no-monitor removes automatic health supervision.
  • Unknown browser-created assignments are not adopted or stopped.

Related commands: rajai-colab status · rajai-colab logs · rajai-colab repair · rajai-colab stop

Lifecycle

rajai-colab status

Displays lifecycle, runtime, model, service health, manifest signature, Vault availability, supervisor, and optional diagnostics.

Syntax

rajai-colab status [--verbose]

What the command does

  • Loads local lifecycle state.
  • Checks the named Colab session.
  • Checks backend/public health and authenticated status.
  • Checks the GitHub manifest signature.
  • Optionally prints detailed JSON and recent failures.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
--verboseOptional flagInclude raw Colab status, manifest JSON, health details, and recent failure events.False

Examples

Example 1: Concise status

rajai-colab status

Best for frequent operational checks.

Example 2: Detailed diagnostics

rajai-colab status --verbose

Use when runtime, tunnel, manifest, or Vault health is unclear.

Example 3: Watch status every 30 seconds

watch -n 30 rajai-colab status

Continuously refreshes a concise status view.

Expected outcomes
  • Returns 0 when no lifecycle is active and no stray named session exists, or when the active service is healthy.
  • Returns 1 when a named VM exists without local state or the active service is unhealthy.

Related commands: rajai-colab logs · rajai-colab repair · rajai-colab doctor

Identity and Access

rajai-colab key

Prints the disposable guest lifecycle key, or the private owner key when --owner is specified.

Syntax

rajai-colab key [--owner]

What the command does

  • Loads the protected local lifecycle state.
  • Selects guest or owner key.
  • Prints the key only.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
--ownerOptional flagPrint the owner key with Personal Memory Vault capabilities instead of the guest key.False

Examples

Example 1: Print the guest key

rajai-colab key

Share only with intended guest users.

Example 2: Print the private owner key

rajai-colab key --owner

Use only on a trusted owner browser; never share it.

Example 3: Copy the guest key into the clipboard when xclip exists

rajai-colab key | xclip -selection clipboard

Copies the guest key without printing it into another application.

Cautions
  • The owner key can access private Vault features.
  • Both keys expire when the lifecycle is restarted or keys are rotated.
  • Avoid screenshots and shell-history exposure.

Related commands: rajai-colab rotate-key · rajai-colab restart · rajai-colab status

Lifecycle

rajai-colab open

Opens the permanent GitHub Pages URL using the default local web browser and prints the URL.

Syntax

rajai-colab open

What the command does

  • Loads public_ui_url from config.toml.
  • Invokes the local default browser.
  • Prints the URL for manual use.

Arguments and options

No command-specific arguments.

Examples

Example 1: Open the interface

rajai-colab open

Launches the fixed RajAIAssist page.

Example 2: Open only after a healthy status

rajai-colab status && rajai-colab open

Prevents opening the page when status reports failure.

Example 3: Print and save the fixed URL

rajai-colab open | tee ~/Documents/rajai-url.txt

Opens the page and records the URL.

Related commands: rajai-colab start --open · rajai-colab key · rajai-colab status

Lifecycle

rajai-colab logs

Displays the local availability-supervisor log and optionally retrieves active-provider process, health, and remote log information.

Syntax

rajai-colab logs [-n LINES] [--provider] [--follow]

What the command does

  • Reads the local supervisor log.
  • Optionally executes the remote probe and prints remote logs.
  • Optionally follows the local supervisor log until interrupted.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
-n, --lines LINESOptional integerNumber of trailing lines to show from each log.160
--providerOptional flagAlso query the active Colab provider and show remote process/health logs.False
--followOptional flagFollow the local supervisor log with tail -f. Ctrl+C stops only the log view.False

Examples

Example 1: Show the latest supervisor messages

rajai-colab logs -n 100

Displays the most recent 100 local supervisor lines.

Example 2: Include remote backend, Ollama/TPU, and tunnel logs

rajai-colab logs --provider -n 200

Use for model-load, Flask, Cloudflare, or bootstrap failures.

Example 3: Follow ongoing availability events

rajai-colab logs --follow --provider

Prints the provider snapshot, then follows the supervisor log.

Related commands: rajai-colab status --verbose · rajai-colab repair · rajai-colab doctor

Back to contents

Lifecycle

rajai-colab repair

Attempts to repair the current provider services while preserving lifecycle keys; when provider repair fails, it can request a replacement of the same selected runtime.

Syntax

rajai-colab repair [--quiet]

What the command does

  • Loads active lifecycle state.
  • Attempts service-level repair and republishing.
  • On failure, publishes offline and starts the configured selected runtime sequence.
  • Preserves the supervisor PID and lifecycle keys when possible.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
--quietOptional flagReduce streamed bootstrap/repair output.False

Prerequisites

  • A local lifecycle state must exist.
  • The bound account and GitHub token must remain valid.

Examples

Example 1: Interactive repair

rajai-colab repair

Shows remote upload/bootstrap progress.

Example 2: Quiet repair

rajai-colab repair --quiet

Useful when only the final result is needed.

Example 3: Inspect, repair, and verify

rajai-colab status --verbose
rajai-colab repair
rajai-colab status --verbose

Captures before-and-after state.

Cautions
  • If the old CLI session is lost but an untracked browser assignment still exists, replacement allocation is refused.
  • Repair does not adopt unknown browser-created runtimes.

Related commands: rajai-colab logs --provider · rajai-colab status · rajai-colab restart

Back to contents

Identity and Access

rajai-colab rotate-key

Rotates both owner and guest lifecycle keys by stopping and rebuilding the selected provider while keeping the current runtime/model policy.

Syntax

rajai-colab rotate-key

What the command does

  • Publishes the old endpoint offline.
  • Stops the provider.
  • Creates fresh owner and guest lifecycle keys.
  • Starts the same selected runtime/model and republishes the endpoint.

Arguments and options

No command-specific arguments.

Examples

Example 1: Rotate after accidental guest-key disclosure

rajai-colab rotate-key

Invalidates the old guest and owner keys.

Example 2: Rotate and retrieve the new guest key

rajai-colab rotate-key
rajai-colab key

Starts the new lifecycle and prints the new guest key.

Example 3: Rotate and verify both modes

rajai-colab rotate-key
rajai-colab key
rajai-colab key --owner
rajai-colab status --verbose

Checks new keys and endpoint publication.

Cautions
  • This restarts the provider and can require a new allocation.
  • Users must enter the new key after rotation.

Related commands: rajai-colab key · rajai-colab restart · rajai-colab stop

Back to contents

Lifecycle

rajai-colab stop

Publishes the endpoint offline, stops the selected Colab provider and supervisor, clears local lifecycle state, and leaves the persistent configuration, secrets, Drive data, and Vault intact.

Syntax

rajai-colab stop [--force]

What the command does

  • Stops the supervisor first to prevent a manifest race.
  • Publishes offline state when credentials are available.
  • Stops the named provider.
  • Removes local lifecycle state.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
--forceOptional flagContinue cleanup even when loading required secrets fails.False

Examples

Example 1: Normal clean shutdown

rajai-colab stop

Recommended at the end of every lifecycle.

Example 2: Force cleanup after credential/config trouble

rajai-colab stop --force

Attempts local and named-session cleanup even when secrets cannot be loaded.

Example 3: Stop and confirm

rajai-colab stop
rajai-colab status

Verifies that the local lifecycle is no longer active.

Related commands: rajai-colab restart · rajai-colab start · rajai-colab status

Back to contents

Lifecycle

rajai-colab restart

Stops the current lifecycle and starts a fresh selected runtime with new owner and guest keys.

Syntax

rajai-colab restart [--runtime t4|cpu|tpu-v5e1] [--model MODEL] [--context TOKENS] [--max-output TOKENS] [--no-drive] [--no-monitor] [--open]

What the command does

  • Runs a forced clean stop.
  • Invokes start with the supplied overrides.
  • Generates new lifecycle keys and endpoint signatures.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
--runtime TYPEOptional valueRuntime provider for the new lifecycle. Accepted values / range: t4, cpu, tpu-v5e1.config.toml default_runtime
--model MODELOptional valueModel alias/tag or TPU identifier.Runtime-specific default.
--context TOKENSOptional integerContext override for the new lifecycle.Runtime-specific default.
--max-output TOKENSOptional integerOutput ceiling override for the new lifecycle.Runtime-specific maximum.
--no-driveOptional flagSkip Drive mounting.False
--no-monitorOptional flagDo not launch the detached supervisor.False
--openOptional flagOpen the fixed UI after startup.False

Examples

Example 1: Fresh T4 general lifecycle

rajai-colab restart --runtime t4 --model general

Stops the old lifecycle and starts qwen3:8b on T4.

Example 2: Switch immediately to the coding model

rajai-colab restart --runtime t4 --model coding --context 32768 --max-output 8192

Creates a new coding-focused lifecycle and new keys.

Example 3: Restart in explicit CPU mode

rajai-colab restart --runtime cpu --model cpu --open

Starts qwen3:1.7b on a standard Colab CPU runtime.

Cautions
  • Restart always changes the owner and guest keys.
  • A new runtime allocation may fail even when the old runtime was healthy.

Related commands: rajai-colab stop · rajai-colab start · rajai-colab rotate-key

Lists built-in T4/CPU Ollama aliases, experimental TPU aliases, configured defaults, and the active lifecycle model.

Syntax

rajai-colab models list

What the command does

No command-specific arguments.

Examples

Example 1: List all aliases

rajai-colab models list

Shows general, fast, coding, reasoning, cpu, and TPU aliases.

Example 2: Save the alias list

rajai-colab models list > ~/Documents/rajai-models.txt

Models

rajai-colab models current

Shows the configured default models for T4, CPU, and TPU, plus the active lifecycle model when one exists.

Syntax

rajai-colab models current

What the command does

  • Loads config.
  • Loads optional lifecycle state.
  • Prints all defaults and active model.

Arguments and options

No command-specific arguments.

Examples

Example 1: Show current model configuration

rajai-colab models current

Displays configured and active models.

Example 2: Check before a restart

rajai-colab models current
rajai-colab restart --runtime t4

Confirms which default will be used when no model override is supplied.

Example 3: Record the model state

rajai-colab models current | tee ~/Documents/rajai-model-state.txt

Models

rajai-colab models set

Changes the persistent T4/Ollama default model in config.toml. It does not switch the currently active lifecycle.

Syntax

rajai-colab models set MODEL

What the command does

  • Resolves an Ollama alias or exact tag.
  • Rejects TPU-only aliases.
  • Writes the new default_model.
  • Prints the restart command required to switch immediately.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
MODELRequired positional valueBuilt-in Ollama alias or exact Ollama model tag. Accepted values / range: Examples: general, coding, qwen3:8b, llama3.1:8b.None

Examples

Example 1: Set the general model by exact tag

rajai-colab models set qwen3:8b

Makes qwen3:8b the persistent T4 default.

Example 2: Set the coding alias

rajai-colab models set coding

Resolves coding to qwen2.5-coder:7b.

Example 3: Set and switch now

rajai-colab models set llama3.1:8b
rajai-colab restart --runtime t4 --model llama3.1:8b

Persists the default and restarts immediately.

Cautions
  • The active lifecycle remains unchanged until restart/start.
  • TPU model selection is done with start --runtime tpu-v5e1 --model ...

Related commands: rajai-colab models current · rajai-colab models verify · rajai-colab restart

Models

rajai-colab models verify

Validates a model tag and, when a lifecycle is active, queries the remote model server to check whether the model is available.

Syntax

rajai-colab models verify MODEL

What the command does

  • Validates model syntax.
  • If no lifecycle is active, stops after local validation.
  • If active, queries Ollama or the TPU tag endpoint and prints installed model names.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
MODELRequired positional valueOllama alias/tag to validate. On TPU, the active provider determines the target server.None

Examples

Example 1: Validate the general model

rajai-colab models verify qwen3:8b

Checks syntax and remote availability when a runtime is active.

Example 2: Verify the coding alias target

rajai-colab models verify qwen2.5-coder:7b

Useful before restarting to the coding model.

Example 3: Verify after startup

rajai-colab start --runtime t4 --model general
rajai-colab models verify qwen3:8b

Confirms the remote model list after bootstrap.

Related commands: rajai-colab models list · rajai-colab start · rajai-colab status

Memory Vault

rajai-colab vault init

Initializes or verifies the owner-only Zorin-canonical Local-First Vault and discovers new files under incoming collection folders.

Syntax

rajai-colab vault init

What the command does

  • Creates or verifies the owner-only local Vault layout under ~/RajAI/Vault.
  • Creates the canonical export, pending-source queue, local manifest, snapshots, journal, backups, and incoming folders.
  • Discovers new files under incoming/<collection>/.
  • When a runtime is active, optionally synchronizes the local snapshot and pending sources.

Arguments and options

No command-specific arguments.

Prerequisites

  • A writable local Vault root, normally ~/RajAI/Vault.
  • An active owner runtime is optional; initialization also works fully offline.

Examples

Example 1: Initialize the Vault

rajai-colab vault init

Safe to run repeatedly.

Example 2: Initialize and inspect status

rajai-colab vault init
rajai-colab vault status

Verifies persistent/cache locations and counts.

Example 3: Initialize after a fresh Drive-backed lifecycle

rajai-colab start --runtime t4 --model general
rajai-colab vault init

Creates the Vault after runtime startup.

Related commands: rajai-colab vault status · rajai-colab vault ingest

Back to contents

Memory Vault

rajai-colab vault status

Reports Vault availability, cache/persistent paths, records, approved memories, sources, chunks, Inbox counts, and collections.

Syntax

rajai-colab vault status

What the command does

  • Reads the canonical Zorin Vault manifest and synchronization state.
  • Reports records, sources, pending files, snapshots, incoming folders, and last sync.
  • If a lifecycle is active, also reports the runtime provider and cache location.

Arguments and options

No command-specific arguments.

Examples

Example 1: Check Vault health

rajai-colab vault status

Displays availability and counts.

Example 2: Save a Vault inventory snapshot

rajai-colab vault status > ~/Documents/rajai-vault-status.json

Records counts and paths.

Example 3: Gate a Vault workflow

if rajai-colab vault status >/dev/null; then
  rajai-colab vault search "project decision" --limit 5
fi

Searches only when the status call succeeds.

Related commands: rajai-colab vault init · rajai-colab status --verbose · rajai-colab vault export

Back to contents

Memory Vault

rajai-colab vault ingest

Copies a local file into the canonical Zorin Vault, queues it by content hash, and synchronizes it to the active Colab cache for extraction, OCR, book processing, and evidence indexing when available.

Syntax

rajai-colab vault ingest --file PATH [--collection NAME] [--title TITLE] [--book] [--ocr auto|always|never] [--ocr-language LANG] [--ocr-dpi DPI] [--sensitivity LEVEL] [--sync|--no-sync]

What the command does

  • Resolves and validates the local path and collection name.
  • Copies the source into managed owner-only Zorin storage and calculates SHA-256.
  • Queues the source without requiring an active runtime.
  • If an owner runtime is active, uploads only pending sources for extraction, OCR, book processing, and indexing.
  • Pulls the completed source evidence back into the canonical Zorin Vault.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
--file PATHRequired valueFile path on the Zorin laptop. ~ is expanded and the file must exist.None
--collection NAMEOptional valueLogical Vault collection.documents
--title TITLEOptional valueHuman-readable source title.Local filename stem.
--bookOptional flagEnable book/chapter-aware metadata processing.False
--ocr MODEOptional valueOCR policy. Accepted values / range: auto, always, never.config.toml vault_ocr_mode
--ocr-language LANGOptional valueTesseract language code.config.toml vault_ocr_language, normally eng
--ocr-dpi DPIOptional integerPDF rendering DPI for OCR. Accepted values / range: 100–400.config.toml vault_ocr_dpi, normally 200
--sensitivity LEVELOptional valueClassification metadata for the source. Accepted values / range: public, shared, private, highly-sensitive.private
--syncOptional flagRequire immediate synchronization when a runtime is active.False
--no-syncOptional flagQueue the source locally without contacting the active runtime.False

Examples

Example 1: Ingest project notes

rajai-colab vault ingest \
  --file ~/Documents/project-notes.pdf \
  --collection projects \
  --title "Project notes" \
  --sensitivity private

Extracts and indexes a normal project document.

Example 2: Ingest a searchable or scanned book

rajai-colab vault ingest \
  --file ~/Books/book.pdf \
  --collection books \
  --book \
  --ocr auto

Uses embedded text and OCRs low-text pages when needed.

Example 3: Force OCR on a screenshot or scan

rajai-colab vault ingest \
  --file ~/Pictures/service-centre.png \
  --collection tiago \
  --title "Service centre screenshot" \
  --ocr always \
  --ocr-language eng \
  --sensitivity private

Runs OCR even when the file contains some embedded metadata.

Cautions
  • Original binary source retention depends on the backend implementation; keep your originals separately.
  • Large OCR jobs can take a long time.
  • Sensitivity is classification metadata, not separate encryption.

Related commands: rajai-colab vault compile · rajai-colab vault search · rajai-colab vault status

Back to contents

Memory Vault

rajai-colab vault compile

Rebuilds compiled metadata/indexes for selected Vault sources and can optionally ask the active model to create chapter/source summaries.

Syntax

rajai-colab vault compile [--collection NAME] [--source-id ID] [--summarize]

What the command does

  • Selects sources by collection, source ID, or all when neither filter is supplied.
  • Builds deterministic compiled metadata.
  • Optionally runs model-generated summaries.
  • Persists compilation results.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
--collection NAMEOptional valueCompile all sources in one collection.All collections when no source-id is supplied.
--source-id IDOptional valueCompile one exact source.All matching collection sources.
--summarizeOptional flagUse the active model to create source/chapter summaries; can be slow and consumes model time.False

Examples

Example 1: Compile all books deterministically

rajai-colab vault compile --collection books

Builds book metadata without model-generated summaries.

Example 2: Compile one exact source

rajai-colab vault compile --source-id src_0123456789abcdef01234567

Limits the operation to one ingested source.

Example 3: Compile and summarize a book collection

rajai-colab vault compile --collection books --summarize

Runs the active model for progressive summaries; schedule when the GPU is otherwise idle.

Related commands: rajai-colab vault ingest · rajai-colab vault search · rajai-colab logs --provider

Back to contents

Memory Vault

rajai-colab vault search

Searches approved structured memories and compiled Vault source evidence using the owner-only retrieval endpoint.

Syntax

rajai-colab vault search QUERY [--collection NAME] [--limit N]

What the command does

  • Builds a query-string request.
  • Optionally restricts retrieval to one collection.
  • Prints ranked source/memory results with labels and text.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
QUERYRequired positional valueSearch text. Quote it when it contains spaces or shell-special characters.None
--collection NAMEOptional valueRestrict results to one Vault collection.All eligible collections.
--limit NOptional integerMaximum number of results. Accepted values / range: Backend accepts up to its configured maximum, commonly 30..8

Examples

Example 1: Search one decisions collection

rajai-colab vault search \
  "Why did we remove the local CPU fallback?" \
  --collection decisions \
  --limit 8

Reduces unrelated retrieval by scoping the collection.

Example 2: Find a unique book identifier

rajai-colab vault search "LUMEN-204" --collection books --limit 12

Exact names and identifiers work well with lexical retrieval.

Example 3: Search across eligible collections

rajai-colab vault search "complete replacement files" --limit 5

Returns approved memories and source chunks from the broad Vault.

Cautions
  • Current search is primarily lexical; explicit names, IDs, dates, and phrases improve accuracy.
  • Use collection scoping to avoid unrelated sources.

Related commands: rajai-colab vault list · rajai-colab vault ingest · rajai-colab vault status

Memory Vault

rajai-colab vault list

Lists structured memory records by collection and lifecycle status.

Syntax

rajai-colab vault list [--collection NAME] [--status STATUS]

What the command does

  • Calls the owner-only memory listing endpoint.
  • Applies optional collection and status filters.
  • Prints memory IDs, content, versioning, provenance, and metadata.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
--collection NAMEOptional valueRestrict records to one collection.All collections.
--status STATUSOptional valueFilter by memory status. Accepted values / range: Common values: approved, pending, superseded, forgotten, rejected.approved

Examples

Example 1: List approved preferences

rajai-colab vault list --collection preferences

Shows current approved preference memories.

Example 2: Inspect superseded versions

rajai-colab vault list --collection preferences --status superseded

Displays records replaced by a correction.

Example 3: Review forgotten records

rajai-colab vault list --status forgotten

Audits memories that are excluded from normal retrieval.

Related commands: rajai-colab vault remember · rajai-colab vault correct · rajai-colab vault forget

Memory Vault

rajai-colab vault remember

Creates an explicit owner-approved memory record. It bypasses the suggestion Inbox because the owner entered it directly.

Syntax

rajai-colab vault remember TEXT [--collection NAME] [--title TITLE] [--sensitivity LEVEL] [--valid-from DATE]

What the command does

  • Builds a verified memory payload.
  • Stores provenance as an explicit user memory.
  • Creates an approved record and prints its memory ID.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
TEXTRequired positional valueMemory content. Quote multi-word text.None
--collection NAMEOptional valueLogical memory collection.personal
--title TITLEOptional valueHuman-readable memory title.Empty
--sensitivity LEVELOptional valueClassification metadata. Accepted values / range: public, shared, private, highly-sensitive.private
--valid-from DATEOptional valueDate/time from which the memory should be considered valid. Accepted values / range: ISO date or timestamp is recommended..Empty/current context

Examples

Example 1: Record a delivery preference

rajai-colab vault remember \
  "Use complete replacement files rather than partial patches." \
  --collection preferences \
  --title "Preferred delivery format" \
  --sensitivity private

Creates an immediately approved preference.

Example 2: Record a dated architecture decision

rajai-colab vault remember \
  "Local Zorin inference is disabled because sustained CPU load was unsuitable." \
  --collection decisions \
  --title "Disable local CPU fallback" \
  --valid-from 2026-07-15

Adds a temporal decision record.

Example 3: Record a project fact

rajai-colab vault remember \
  "Project Lumen review is scheduled for 18 August 2026." \
  --collection projects \
  --title "Project Lumen review"

Stores a project timeline fact.

Cautions
  • Do not store passwords, access tokens, private keys, OTPs, or banking credentials.

Related commands: rajai-colab vault list · rajai-colab vault correct · rajai-colab vault forget

Back to contents

Memory Vault

rajai-colab vault correct

Creates a corrected memory version while retaining the previous record as superseded history.

Syntax

rajai-colab vault correct MEMORY_ID TEXT [--title TITLE]

What the command does

  • Loads the referenced approved memory.
  • Creates a new approved version.
  • Marks the original as superseded and links version history.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
MEMORY_IDRequired positional valueExact memory ID returned by remember, list, or approval.None
TEXTRequired positional valueCorrected memory content.None
--title TITLEOptional valueReplacement title.Backend keeps or derives a title when empty.

Examples

Example 1: Correct a preference

rajai-colab vault correct \
  mem_0123456789abcdef01234567 \
  "Use complete replacement files, and include a concise patch for review."

Creates a version-2 approved memory.

Example 2: Correct and retitle a decision

rajai-colab vault correct \
  mem_0123456789abcdef01234567 \
  "The T4-only policy uses an initial request plus one retry after 60 seconds." \
  --title "Current T4 allocation policy"

Updates both content and title.

Example 3: Capture the new memory ID

NEW_ID=$(rajai-colab vault correct mem_OLD "Corrected text" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["record"]["id"])')
echo "$NEW_ID"

Extracts the replacement ID for later lifecycle operations.

Related commands: rajai-colab vault list --status superseded · rajai-colab vault forget · rajai-colab vault search

Back to contents

Memory Vault

rajai-colab vault forget

Marks a memory as forgotten so it is excluded from normal retrieval while retaining the audit and historical record.

Syntax

rajai-colab vault forget MEMORY_ID

What the command does

  • Authenticates as owner.
  • Sends a DELETE request for the memory lifecycle operation.
  • Sets forgotten/valid-to metadata rather than silently losing audit history.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
MEMORY_IDRequired positional valueExact approved memory ID to forget.None

Examples

Example 1: Forget one obsolete preference

rajai-colab vault forget mem_0123456789abcdef01234567

Removes it from normal approved retrieval.

Example 2: Verify the forgotten state

rajai-colab vault forget mem_0123456789abcdef01234567
rajai-colab vault list --status forgotten

Confirms lifecycle status.

Example 3: Forget the corrected version stored in a shell variable

rajai-colab vault forget "$NEW_MEMORY_ID"

Useful after capturing a replacement ID from correct.

Cautions
  • Forget is a logical lifecycle operation, not necessarily physical erasure from audit/backups.

Related commands: rajai-colab vault correct · rajai-colab vault list · rajai-colab vault export

Memory Vault

rajai-colab vault suggest

Reviews one browser chat with the active model and creates owner-reviewable candidate memories in the Vault Inbox.

Syntax

rajai-colab vault suggest --session-id BROWSER_SESSION_ID [--max-items N]

What the command does

  • Loads recent chat history for the session.
  • Asks the model for durable user-confirmed facts, preferences, goals, decisions, procedures, or events.
  • Filters likely credentials.
  • Stores candidates as pending Inbox items.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
--session-id IDRequired valueFull browser session ID. Obtain it from localStorage.getItem("rajai_session_id") in the page console.None
--max-items NOptional integerMaximum candidate memories to request. Accepted values / range: Current backend maximum is typically 12..8

Examples

Example 1: Suggest up to eight memories

rajai-colab vault suggest --session-id FULL_BROWSER_SESSION_ID

Uses the default candidate limit.

Example 2: Limit the review to five candidates

rajai-colab vault suggest --session-id FULL_BROWSER_SESSION_ID --max-items 5

Reduces review workload.

Example 3: Review Inbox immediately afterward

rajai-colab vault suggest --session-id FULL_BROWSER_SESSION_ID --max-items 8
rajai-colab vault inbox

Creates candidates and lists them for approval.

Cautions
  • Suggestions are not approved facts until the owner explicitly approves them.
  • The model can still propose a bad candidate; review every item.

Related commands: rajai-colab vault inbox · rajai-colab vault decide · rajai-colab vault remember

Memory Vault

rajai-colab vault inbox

Lists model-suggested memory candidates and their review status.

Syntax

rajai-colab vault inbox

What the command does

  • Authenticates with the owner key.
  • Queries the Vault Inbox.
  • Prints candidate IDs, content, confidence, collection, provenance, and status.

Arguments and options

No command-specific arguments.

Examples

Example 1: Review all Inbox items

rajai-colab vault inbox

Shows pending, approved, or rejected suggestions retained by the backend.

Example 2: Save an Inbox review copy

rajai-colab vault inbox > ~/Documents/rajai-memory-inbox.json

Creates a review artifact.

Example 3: Review after chat suggestion

rajai-colab vault suggest --session-id FULL_BROWSER_SESSION_ID
rajai-colab vault inbox

Generates and then lists candidates.

Related commands: rajai-colab vault suggest · rajai-colab vault decide · rajai-colab vault list

Back to contents

Memory Vault

rajai-colab vault decide

Approves or rejects one pending Inbox memory. Approval creates a separate approved memory record; rejection keeps only audit history.

Syntax

rajai-colab vault decide MEMORY_ID (--approve | --reject)

What the command does

  • Selects one mutually exclusive action.
  • Calls the owner-only approval/rejection endpoint.
  • Prints the resulting Inbox and approved-record metadata.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
MEMORY_IDRequired positional valueInbox item ID returned by vault inbox.None
--approveRequired choiceApprove the candidate and create an approved Vault memory.Mutually exclusive with --reject.
--rejectRequired choiceReject the candidate so it is not used as approved memory.Mutually exclusive with --approve.

Examples

Example 1: Approve a candidate

rajai-colab vault decide mem_0123456789abcdef01234567 --approve

Creates an approved memory with a new permanent ID.

Example 2: Reject a candidate

rajai-colab vault decide mem_0123456789abcdef01234567 --reject

Prevents the suggestion from entering approved retrieval.

Example 3: Approve and verify the final record

rajai-colab vault decide mem_0123456789abcdef01234567 --approve
rajai-colab vault list --collection preferences

Finds the approved memory in its collection.

Related commands: rajai-colab vault inbox · rajai-colab vault list · rajai-colab vault correct

Memory Vault

rajai-colab vault export

Writes the current canonical Zorin Vault manifest, structured memories, source metadata/chunks, and Inbox as one protected JSON export.

Syntax

rajai-colab vault export --output PATH

What the command does

  • Reads the canonical Local-First export from Zorin.
  • Creates parent directories when needed.
  • Writes UTF-8 pretty-printed JSON and restricts the output to the owner where supported.

Arguments and options

ArgumentRequirementDescription and accepted valuesDefault
--output PATHRequired valueLocal Zorin destination for the JSON export. ~ is expanded.None

Examples

Example 1: Export to Documents

rajai-colab vault export --output ~/Documents/rajai-vault-export.json

Creates the standard local backup file.

Example 2: Create a dated export

rajai-colab vault export --output ~/Documents/rajai-vault-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).json

Preserves multiple snapshots.

Example 3: Export and restrict permissions

rajai-colab vault export --output ~/Documents/rajai-vault-export.json
chmod 600 ~/Documents/rajai-vault-export.json

Protects the sensitive export from other local users.

Cautions
  • Exports can contain private memories and extracted source text.
  • The current export may not contain original binary files.

Related commands: rajai-colab vault status · rajai-colab vault list · rajai-colab vault ingest

Back to contents

Local-First Vault

rajai-colab vault sync

Synchronizes the Zorin-canonical Vault with the temporary Vault cache inside the active Colab runtime.

Syntax

rajai-colab vault sync {status|push|pull|both}
ArgumentMeaning
statusShow the canonical local Vault and active runtime-cache state without changing either side.
pushPush the canonical structured snapshot and all pending source files to Colab. Use after adding local files or memories.
pullDownload and merge runtime-created memories, OCR, compiled book data, and Inbox decisions into Zorin.
bothPush local state and pending sources, then pull the merged runtime Vault back to Zorin.

What happens internally

  1. Loads the private owner key and active endpoint.
  2. Verifies an owner-authenticated runtime is online.
  3. Transfers the requested snapshot, pending sources, or export.
  4. Merges by stable memory/source identifiers.
  5. Updates local sync timestamps atomically.
Example 1 — inspect sync state
rajai-colab vault sync status
Example 2 — send locally added material
rajai-colab vault sync push
Example 3 — reconcile both directions
rajai-colab vault sync both
Important Pull before stopping whenever valuable OCR or compilation work occurred. A Colab VM can disappear without warning.
Related: vault status, vault ingest, stop, status --verbose.
Local-First Vault

rajai-colab vault import-chat

Imports an exported conversation transcript as source evidence, optionally redacts credential-like text, and queues it for runtime ingestion.

Syntax

rajai-colab vault import-chat --file FILE [--source LABEL] [--collection NAME] [--title TEXT] [--redact-secrets|--no-redact-secrets] [--no-sync]
ArgumentDescriptionDefault
--file FILERequired local HTML, Markdown, text, or exported conversation file.Required
--source LABELPlatform/source label such as chatgpt, slack, or notes.chatgpt
--collection NAMELowercase Vault collection name.conversations
--title TEXTHuman-readable source title.Input filename stem
--redact-secretsReplace likely tokens, passwords, bearer values, OAuth codes, and private keys before storage.Enabled
--no-redact-secretsDisable automated redaction. Use only after manual review.False
--no-syncQueue locally but do not send to an active runtime immediately.False

What happens internally

  1. Removes script/style markup and converts HTML to searchable text.
  2. Runs credential-pattern redaction when enabled.
  3. Copies the cleaned transcript into managed Zorin source storage.
  4. Calculates SHA-256 and queues it by collection.
  5. Synchronizes immediately when an owner runtime is online, unless --no-sync is used.
Example 1 — import ChatGPT history safely
rajai-colab vault import-chat \ --file ~/Documents/rajai-thread.html \ --source chatgpt \ --collection conversations \ --title "RajAIAssist development history" \ --redact-secrets
Example 2 — queue an offline Markdown transcript
rajai-colab vault import-chat \ --file ~/Documents/project-chat.md \ --source notes \ --collection projects \ --no-sync
Example 3 — import a reviewed plain-text archive
rajai-colab vault import-chat \ --file ~/Documents/team-history.txt \ --source slack \ --collection conversations \ --title "Team history"
Trust rule A transcript is source evidence, not automatically approved personal memory. Use the Memory Inbox to review durable facts and decisions.

Exit Codes and Failure Handling

CodeMeaningTypical examples
0Successful command or healthy/ready result.doctor ready; healthy status; successful Vault request.
1General operational, validation, configuration, service, or authentication error.Invalid config; wrong account; unhealthy service; Vault HTTP failure.
2Allocation diagnostic failed after a real probe.T4 probe returned capacity/quota/control-plane failure.
130User cancelled or interrupted an operation.Ctrl+C or declining the interactive allocation diagnostic.

Unexpected exceptions are normally summarized as Unexpected error: TYPE: message. Set RAJAI_DEBUG=1 only during private troubleshooting when a full Python traceback is required.

Operational Cheat Sheet

Setup and identity

rajai-colab --version
rajai-colab migrate-config --force
rajai-colab auth --reset --email ACCOUNT@gmail.com
rajai-colab doctor

Start and operate

rajai-colab start --runtime t4 --model general
rajai-colab status --verbose
rajai-colab key
rajai-colab key --owner
rajai-colab open
rajai-colab logs --follow --provider

Recovery and shutdown

rajai-colab repair
rajai-colab rotate-key
rajai-colab restart --runtime t4 --model coding
rajai-colab stop

Models

rajai-colab models list
rajai-colab models current
rajai-colab models set qwen3:8b
rajai-colab models verify qwen3:8b

Vault

rajai-colab vault init
rajai-colab vault status
rajai-colab vault ingest --file FILE --collection projects --ocr auto
rajai-colab vault compile --collection books --summarize
rajai-colab vault search "QUERY" --collection projects --limit 8
rajai-colab vault remember "TEXT" --collection preferences
rajai-colab vault inbox
rajai-colab vault export --output ~/Documents/rajai-vault.json
